findings.title: At write: false the basic content forbids the replacement a walk must write for a reading finding on a record written earlier
findings.recommendation: The basic content says that on `write: false` the agent writes "no ledger entry, stop record or resolution". address-reviews, which carries the same basic content, resolves a reading finding (`pass: "reading"`) ONLY by writing a replacement record through `orbit emit <ledger|stop|resolution>` (address-reviews.ts:1249). The reading step selects every unread record whatever the settings (`selectUnreadRecords`, decision-records.ts:716), so records written before this change lands, or while a setting was on and later turned off, are still selected and read at the defaults. This change's own trail is that case: `orbit/changes/records-by-setting/.orbit-runs/decisions/` holds five ledger entries, and `node bin/orbit.js decisions brief records-by-setting` selects them today. After task 4.1 (`update --force`) the system review's reading step will read them, and a finding on any of them meets a walk whose body forbids its only fix. The design's premise is stated as fact in three places: design.md:15-16 ("at the defaults nothing is" written), design.md:132-134 (D-rbs-7: "its system review, walk and archive write none, which is correct here, since nothing reads them"), and the orbit-decision-records delta at lines 25-26 (the reading step reads "what was written, which at the defaults is nothing"). Pick one rule, state it in the basic content and in the rule's fence, and correct the three premise sentences.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Narrow the prohibition to new records: "on `write: false`, write no new ledger entry, stop record or resolution; a replacement a walk writes to fix a reading finding is still written". Keep the fence and its parity pin in step, and correct design.md:15-16, design.md:132-134 and the orbit-decision-records delta at 25-26 so they say that records already in a trail are still read and fixed at the defaults.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Keep the blanket prohibition and give the walk a defined outcome: at `write: false` a reading finding on a record is resolved `deferred`, naming this limit, and no replacement is written. State the limit in `Decision-writing discipline` and correct the same three premise sentences.

findings.reproduction: Constructed case (proposal mode): (1) Today `node bin/orbit.js decisions brief records-by-setting` renders a brief over five ledger records in this change's decisions/ folder. (2) Apply runs task 4.1, so this repository's bodies carry the basic content and `orbit decisions status --json` reports `write: false` (no chain, signoff or tripwires key in orbit/config.yaml). (3) The in-context system review's reading step selects those five records (selectUnreadRecords does not read chain or tripwires) and the reader flags one as unclear. (4) The /orbit:address-reviews walk reads its basic content (write no ledger entry) and its step for reading findings (write a replacement via orbit emit ledger). Expected: one defined action. Observed: the two instructions conflict, and design.md's D-rbs-7 risk line says this walk writes nothing because nothing reads the records.

findings.title: The deltas still say bodies carry the "rule" or the "statement", which this change moves to the reference
findings.recommendation: The orbit-decision-records ADDED requirement says "every session whose body carries the decision-writing rule runs the same call" (line 70), but after this change the bodies carry the basic content, and the rule lives only in `references/decision-records.md`. The orbit-conventions delta keeps the old word too: `Decision-record reference ships beside the statement` says "Every generated workflow skill whose epitome carries the decision-writing statement SHALL ship" (line 176), and so does its scenario `Every statement-carrying skill ships the reference` (lines 208-212). The `Decision-writing discipline` delta no longer defines "statement": it now has "basic content" and "rule". The generated reference carries the same old word: disciplines.ts:300 says "(each by its gloss in the decision-writing statement)", which, once the rule sits in the reference's first section, should point at "the rule above". Change line 70 to "basic content". In the reference requirement's body and scenario, say "decision-writing basic content" (the title can stay, or take a RENAMED entry). Add the disciplines.ts:300 rewording to task 2.1, and the 2.3 tag move if the scenario is renamed.

findings.title: Task 3.2 adds decision-record claims to customization.md's settings rows without adding their owner to the section's Carried by line
findings.recommendation: docs/customization.md's settings section ends `Carried by: orbit-engine-gates, orbit-pr-lifecycle, orbit-scenario-map, orbit-change-size, orbit-program-brief, orbit-tripwires` (line 93). Task 3.2 makes the `chain`, `signoff` and `tripwires` rows each say which state makes the AI write decision records, a claim `orbit-decision-records` owns (`Decision records are written when a setting reads them`). The Carried by check (`orbit-user-docs`' `Every H2 section of four concept pages declares its owner on a checked Carried by line`) confirms only that each named capability exists, so the suite stays green with the owner missing. Add "and add `orbit-decision-records` to the section's Carried by line" to task 3.2.

findings.title: The moments table leaves out a command the user types later in the same session, a result lost to compaction, and orbit/config.yml
findings.recommendation: The basic content runs the call "at the session's start". The table's members are the session start, the session's own config edit, a chained command, a dispatched worker and an outside edit. A second command the user types later in the same conversation (the body is first loaded mid-session) is not a member. Neither is a result the agent no longer holds after a compaction. A literal reader who loads the body mid-session may decide the start has passed and run nothing, then act with no result. Also, the resolvers read `orbit/config.yml` when `orbit/config.yaml` is absent (project-config.ts:345-349), but the basic content names only `orbit/config.yaml`. One phrasing closes the gaps: "before this command's first step, unless this session already holds the result, and again after this session edits the project config (`orbit/config.yaml` or `.yml`)". It costs one repeated call per command, not per designed moment. Then add the user-typed-command row to the table.

findings.title: The tripwire named limit's "disagree only when a halt is removed after a change's fixed point" misses an uncommitted removal
findings.recommendation: `sensorHalts` (tripwires.ts:229-241) halts when the config at HEAD says `halt`, or the config at the fixed point does. `orbit decisions status` reads the working tree. So a halt removed in the working tree and not yet committed, before any fixed point, also gives `write: false` while the sensor still halts at HEAD. The opposite case, a halt added and not yet committed, gives `write: true` with no halting sensor, which is harmless but is also a disagreement. Reword the limit to name what each side reads (working tree vs HEAD or fixed point) and drop "only", or list both members.

findings.title: Proposal Impact places the predicate in decision-records.ts or project-config.ts, which the design rules out
findings.recommendation: Proposal line 51 says "`src/core/decision-records.ts` (or `project-config.ts`): the predicate". Design Decision 2 and task 1.1 put it in a new `src/core/decision-status.ts`, and say it cannot live in decision-records.ts because tripwires.ts imports that module. Make the Impact line name `src/core/decision-status.ts`.

findings.title: Touchpoints omit src/commands/decisions.ts, where the `decisions` subcommands' actions live
findings.recommendation: `orbit decisions brief` is a thin registration in program.ts that dispatches to `DecisionsCommand` in `src/commands/decisions.ts` (program.ts:373). A `status` action built the same way edits that file, which the Touchpoints list does not name. The Touchpoints sensor is record-only here, but its reading will show the file as unpredicted. Add `src/commands/decisions.ts`, or say in Decision 2 that the action is written inline in program.ts. Also give task 1.2 an update to the `decisions` group's description (program.ts:367, "the brief the reading step gives its reader"), which will no longer describe both subcommands.

findings.title: The two new fences share a first line, and one scenario task 2.3 tags has a behaviour THEN
findings.recommendation: Both fences in `Decision-writing discipline` open `- **Decision-writing (call-time)**:`. The parity test finds its fence with `fencedProduction(owner, '- **Decision-writing (call-time)**')` (decision-writing-parity.test.ts:32, 144-146), which returns the FIRST match: after this change, that is the basic content. Task 2.3 should anchor each fence on a longer prefix (`...: at the session's start` vs `...: when \`orbit decisions status\``). Separately, the THEN of `At the defaults the body directs no record` includes running `orbit decisions status --json` and getting `write: false`, which is a behaviour. Task 2.3 tags it in the parity test without naming the tag kind. Either run the predicate on an empty project there and tag `behaviour`, or keep only the text half in that THEN.

findings.title: Scenario titles use "owed", the word Decision 2 keeps for records owed a reading
findings.recommendation: Design Decision 2 names the fields `write` and `readers` so that "owed" stays the word of the review emit's `decision_records_owed` (records owed a READING). Three new scenario titles bring the word back with the other meaning: `At the defaults no record is owed` (47), `Each reading setting makes records owed` (52), `A setting with no reader owes nothing` (58). Retitle them in the requirement's own word, "written", before task 1.3 tags them.

findings.title: Task 3.3's "rewrite CLAUDE.md's Decision-writing bullet" covers a bullet that also carries the installed-CLI workarounds
findings.recommendation: CLAUDE.md's Decision-writing bullet also carries the workarounds that have nothing to do with decision records: `node bin/orbit.js pr commit`, `brief --save`, `brief --hold`, and `emit signoff` for both the change and doc forms. Narrow task 3.3 to the bullet's decision-record sentences: "keep a decision record …", "The full statement is the fifth epitome bullet in every workflow body", which becomes false, and "write records with node bin/orbit.js emit …". Say that the rest of the bullet stays as it is.

commentary: Read: the four artifacts, explore.md, both deltas against their baselines (the three conventions requirements diffed line by line), the stage charter and R-rop-17, and the code each claim names: the three resolvers, takesAccount, tripwireSensors, sensorHalts, earliestOpenStop, selectUnreadRecords, the parity test's fence lookup and the edit ledger's ONE_PARAGRAPH handling. The predicate is accurate to the code: the three terms match the resolvers' behaviour on absent, unparseable and unrecognized input, and the RENAMED-plus-MODIFIED shape and the edit ledger's undo-first are both sound (only this change's swap touches the fourteen recorded bodies; onboard is not among them). The weak point is one premise. The design treats "at the defaults nothing is written" as "at the defaults nothing is read". But the reading step reads by trail, not by setting, so every in-flight change carrying records, this one included, keeps being read after the switch, and the walk's fix for what it finds is a write. The rest is vocabulary left behind when the rule moved ("statement", "rule" in the bodies, "owed") and task wording that leaves out a known-easy miss (the Carried by owner).

direction.reasoning: The design is ready to build once the walk settles one question: what a walk does at `write: false` when the reading step hands it a record written earlier. Either answer is a sentence in the basic content and its fence, plus three premise corrections, and it matters here first, because this change's own system review will read its five ledger entries. The other findings are wording and task precision that the same walk can take. Nothing in the predicate, the command or the move of the rule needs rethinking.
